key_insight: PITT fuses physics priors with tokenized equation structure to accurately track shocks and preserve steady states in nonlinear balance laws.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more reliable surrogate for wave-dominated fluid simulations where geometry, discontinuities, and long-time shock motion matter.
method: Tokenize the governing PDE and encode it with a Fourier neural operator.
Advance leading discontinuities using the explicit Rankine–Hugoniot shock law.
Learn a correction term for smooth regions, rarefactions, and finite-resolution effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tests on moving shocks, stationary shocks, rarefaction waves, and Burgers-limit cases, with comparisons against a standard high-order finite-volume method.
watch_item: Performance relies on having explicit analytical structure available, so extending the approach to problems without closed-form jump laws or steady states may be harder.
paper_title: Physics-informed token transformer methodology for nonlinear balance laws. I. Schwarzschild--Burgers fluid flows
